title: DS-CORE baseline requirements: distributed HTAP document store
summary: Initial requirement set for DS-CORE: Raft-replicated sharded key-value/document store, serializable transactions, PartiQL API, eventually consistent row-format analytics replicas, plus durability, availability, performance, security and operability baselines. Records 18 research findings and 5 accepted decisions.
rationale: Elicited from the product owner on 2026-10-05 (engine type, HTAP workload, Raft, serializable, p99 targets, analytics freshness, PartiQL) and grounded in standards research (Raft paper, Jepsen analyses, etcd/TiDB/MongoDB/Spanner docs, RFC 8259, BSON, NIST SP 800-52r2). Items not explicitly chosen by the PO use research defaults and are flagged in notes.

data.claim: The Raft paper recommends a 150-300 ms election timeout and requires broadcastTime << electionTimeout << MTBF.
Raft handles membership changes with two-phase joint consensus in which both old and new configurations apply until the joint configuration commits.
Jepsen found TiDB 2.1.7 to 3.0.0-beta.1 exhibited read skew and lost updates due to transaction auto-retry, fixed by disabling retry by default in 3.0.0-rc.2.
Jepsen found MongoDB 4.2.6 transactions defaulted to read concern local and w:1 and showed snapshot isolation violations including read skew.
CockroachDB offers serializable as its only isolation level and documents its guarantee as no stale reads rather than strict serializability.
TiFlash replicas are Raft learners that replicate asynchronously and do not participate in commit quorum.
YCSB core workloads are A update-heavy 50/50, B read-mostly 95/5, C read-only, D read-latest, E short ranges and F read-modify-write.
etcd documents typical fdatasync latency of about 10 ms on spinning disks and under 1 ms on SSDs, and that cluster performance is bounded by network RTT and disk I/O.
TiDB log backup for PITR can reach an RPO as short as five minutes, with about 5% overhead and restore at about 30 GiB per hour per TiKV node.
Cloud Spanner commits 99.999% monthly uptime for multi-region and dual-region instances and 99.99% for regional instances, computed per month per project per region.
TiDB supports online rolling upgrades with leader eviction before node stop and a 5-minute default leader-transfer timeout.
MongoDB limits BSON documents to 16 MiB, nesting to 100 levels and indexes to 64 per collection.
RFC 8259 says JSON object names SHOULD be unique, parser behaviour on duplicates is unpredictable, and exact integer interoperability is only guaranteed within ±(2^53−1).
BSON 1.1 defines int32, int64, double and decimal128 types and does not specify a maximum document size.
JSON Schema 2020-12 is the current stable version and treats the format keyword as annotation-only unless the format-assertion vocabulary is used.
NIST SP 800-52r2 requires TLS servers to support TLS 1.3 by 2024-01-01.
GDPR Article 17 erasure applies to personal data held in storage files, backups, replicas and logs; SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 expect evidence of access control, encryption and logging.
PartiQL (SQL++ family) is a SQL-compatible query language for nested and semi-structured data; not verified against a primary specification.

data.title: Raft replication per shard
data.statement: The system shall replicate every shard using the Raft consensus protocol with an odd number of voting replicas (default 3) placed in distinct availability zones.
data.rationale: PO decision: distributed, sharded, strong consistency via Raft.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every shard has 3 or 5 voting replicas; even voter counts are rejected by configuration validation.
With 3 AZs available, no two voters of the same shard are placed in the same AZ.

data.title: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness
data.statement: The system shall provide the security controls and audit evidence required for SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification.
data.rationale: Research default: common enterprise buyer requirement; FIPS 140-3 deferred until a market requires it.

acceptance_criteria.text: A control matrix maps each SOC 2 Trust Services Criterion and ISO 27001 Annex A control in scope to a DS-CORE requirement or documented exclusion.

data.notes: Not explicitly chosen by the PO; FIPS 140-3 out of scope for v1.

data.title: PartiQL query language
data.statement: The system shall accept queries and data manipulation statements (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) expressed in PartiQL over documents and nested values.
data.rationale: PO decision: SQL++/PartiQL as the primary query API.

acceptance_criteria.text: A published conformance matrix lists every PartiQL feature as supported, partially supported or unsupported.
All statements marked supported in the conformance matrix pass the project's PartiQL conformance test suite.
Unsupported syntax returns a parse error naming the unsupported feature, not a generic failure.

data.title: Versioned client protocol
data.statement: The system shall expose a documented, versioned client protocol for submitting PartiQL statements and controlling transactions (begin, commit, rollback).
data.rationale: PartiQL is a language, not a transport; clients need a stable protocol.

acceptance_criteria.text: The protocol specification is published with a version number, and the server rejects unsupported client protocol versions with a version-mismatch error.
A client can begin, commit and roll back a multi-statement transaction through the protocol.

data.notes: Open: transport choice (gRPC vs. HTTP/2 vs. custom binary) not yet decided.

data.title: Retryable serialization-conflict error
data.statement: The system shall return a distinct, documented retryable error code when a transaction aborts because of a serialization conflict.
data.rationale: Serializable isolation raises abort rates; clients need to distinguish retryable conflicts from permanent failures.

acceptance_criteria.text: A forced write-write conflict between two concurrent transactions returns the documented serialization-conflict code to the aborted client.
Non-retryable failures (syntax, permission, constraint violation) never return the serialization-conflict code.

data.title: Typed document values
data.statement: The system shall store document values with explicit types, including int64, double, decimal128, timestamp, binary, array and nested document, without loss of precision on round trip.
data.rationale: Plain JSON loses integer precision beyond 2^53 and has no decimal type.

acceptance_criteria.text: Writing and reading back int64 values ±(2^63−1) and decimal128 values returns identical values and types.
Documents nested up to 100 levels round-trip unchanged.

data.title: Reject duplicate field names
data.statement: The system shall reject at ingest any document that contains duplicate field names within the same object.
data.rationale: RFC 8259 leaves duplicate-key behaviour undefined; parsers disagree, creating consistency and injection risk.

acceptance_criteria.text: An insert or update containing an object with a repeated field name fails with a validation error and stores nothing.

data.title: Optional per-collection schema validation
data.statement: The system shall reject writes that do not conform to the JSON Schema 2020-12 document attached to their collection.
data.rationale: Lets teams enforce structure where needed while keeping document flexibility; collections without a schema are unvalidated.

acceptance_criteria.text: With a schema attached, a non-conforming insert is rejected with an error naming the failing schema path.
A schema containing a remote (http/https) $ref is rejected when attached.

data.title: Bounded physical erasure
data.statement: The system shall make deleted documents unrecoverable from data files, WAL, replicas and backups within 30 days of deletion.
data.rationale: GDPR Art. 17: deletes in log-structured/replicated engines leave copies in tombstones, WAL, replicas and backups.

acceptance_criteria.text: 30 days after a delete, a byte-level scan of data files, WAL segments and analytics replicas finds no plaintext of the deleted document.
Backups older than the delete become unreadable for the deleted data via destruction of the associated encryption key (crypto-shredding) within 30 days.

data.source: Research default — PO to confirm 30-day bound

data.title: Document size limit
data.statement: The system shall enforce a configurable maximum document size, defaulting to 16 MiB, and reject larger documents with a size-limit error.
data.rationale: Unbounded documents risk memory exhaustion and oversized Raft log entries.

acceptance_criteria.text: With default configuration, a 16 MiB document is accepted and a 16 MiB + 1 byte document is rejected with the size-limit error.
Changing the configured limit takes effect without a cluster restart.

data.title: Serializable isolation by default
data.statement: The system shall execute every transaction, including single-statement and cross-shard transactions, at serializable isolation regardless of session, collection or client settings.
data.rationale: PO decision: serializable by default. Jepsen found weak defaults undercutting advertised guarantees (MongoDB 4.2.6).

acceptance_criteria.text: No session, collection or client option can lower isolation below serializable; attempts return a configuration error.

A Jepsen-style test (network partitions, node crashes, clock skew, membership changes and shard splits) runs for at least 1 hour per release and an Elle-style checker finds zero serializability anomalies.

data.title: Safe internal transaction retry
data.statement: The system shall produce 0 lost updates and 0 serializability anomalies attributable to internal transaction retry.
data.rationale: TiDB's auto-retry caused lost updates and read skew (Jepsen 2.1.7). Retries that cannot preserve serializability must surface the serialization-conflict error instead.

acceptance_criteria.text: An interactive transaction whose read set changed is never silently retried; the client receives the serialization-conflict error.
The Jepsen-style suite run for at least 1 hour with internal retry enabled reports 0 lost updates.

data.title: Durable quorum commit
data.statement: The system shall lose 0 acknowledged writes when every node loses power simultaneously, acknowledging a write only after a majority of the shard's voting replicas have fsynced it.
data.rationale: Prevents loss of acknowledged writes on correlated power loss. Analytics replicas never count toward the quorum.

acceptance_criteria.text: After power-cutting all nodes of a 3-voter shard immediately after acknowledgment, every acknowledged write is present on restart (1,000 trials, zero losses).
With only one voter plus any number of analytics replicas reachable, writes to that shard are not acknowledged.

data.title: Safe membership change
data.statement: The system shall keep at most 1 leader per shard per Raft term in 100% of voter membership changes, using joint consensus or single-server changes.
data.rationale: Single-step multi-voter changes can produce split majorities. New replicas join as non-voting learners and are promoted after catch-up.

acceptance_criteria.text: Under the Jepsen-style suite with continuous add/remove of replicas, no two leaders are observed in the same term for a shard.
A newly added replica is not counted as a voter until its log lag is below the configured bound.

data.title: Leader failover time
data.statement: The system shall elect a new shard leader and resume serving writes within 10 seconds (p99) of the current leader's node failing.
data.rationale: Bounds write unavailability per shard; research found no verified industry figure.

acceptance_criteria.text: Across 100 leader-node kills in a 3-AZ cluster, p99 time from kill to first successful write on the affected shard is ≤ 10 s.
Configuration validation rejects election timeouts less than 10× the measured heartbeat round trip.

data.source: Research — PO to confirm 10 s bound

data.title: Regional availability SLA
data.statement: The system shall achieve at least 99.99% monthly availability for a regional deployment spanning 3 availability zones.
data.rationale: Research default aligned with Spanner regional SLA structure; 99.999% reserved for future multi-region.

acceptance_criteria.text: Availability is measured per calendar month as the fraction of 1-minute intervals in which a synthetic probe's read and write both succeed, and is ≥ 99.99%.
Loss of one full availability zone causes no interval of unavailability longer than the failover bound.

data.title: Point-in-time recovery
data.statement: The system shall restore a cluster to any chosen timestamp within a 7-day retention window, losing no more than 5 minutes of committed transactions.
data.rationale: Quorum replication gives RPO 0 against node loss but not against operator error or corruption.

acceptance_criteria.text: After destroying the cluster, restoring to a chosen timestamp recovers all transactions committed at least 5 minutes before the loss.
Restore throughput is measured and published per node, and the documented RTO formula predicts measured restore time within 20%.

data.title: Rolling upgrade without downtime
data.statement: The system shall upgrade one node at a time between consecutive minor versions while continuing to serve reads and writes, transferring shard leadership off each node before it stops.
data.rationale: Planned maintenance must not consume the availability budget.

acceptance_criteria.text: During a rolling upgrade under YCSB workload A, the synthetic probe records no failed interval and OLTP p99 stays within its target +50%.
A mixed-version cluster of N and N+1 minor versions passes the transaction test suite.

data.title: OLTP point read/write latency
data.statement: The system shall serve single-document point reads within 10 ms and point writes within 20 ms at the 99th percentile in a 3-AZ single-region deployment on SSD storage, at 70% of rated cluster throughput.
data.rationale: PO decision on p99 targets.

acceptance_criteria.text: YCSB workloads A, B, C and F run for 30 minutes each at 70% of rated throughput; p99 read latency ≤ 10 ms.
In the same runs, p99 write (update/read-modify-write) latency ≤ 20 ms.

data.title: OLTP latency under analytical load
data.statement: The system shall keep OLTP p99 latency within 10% of its no-analytics baseline while analytical queries saturate the analytics replicas.
data.rationale: The purpose of dedicated analytics replicas is workload isolation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Running YCSB workload A concurrently with a CH-benCHmark-style analytical load at 100% analytics-replica CPU, OLTP p99 read and write latency increase by no more than 10% versus the same YCSB run without analytics.

data.source: Research default — PO to confirm 10% bound

data.title: Analytics on dedicated replicas
data.statement: The system shall execute queries marked analytical only on dedicated non-voting analytics replicas that store data in the same row/document format as voting replicas.
data.rationale: PO decision: dedicated same-format analytics replicas.

acceptance_criteria.text: An analytical query is never executed on a voting replica; tracing shows only analytics replicas served it.
If no analytics replica is available, an analytical query fails with an explicit error rather than falling back to voting replicas.

data.notes: Open: how a query is marked analytical (hint, session, separate endpoint).

data.title: Eventual consistency of analytics reads
data.statement: The system shall document that analytics-replica reads are eventually consistent, with no freshness bound and no cross-shard snapshot guarantee.
data.rationale: PO decision: eventual, no freshness guarantee. Users must not mistake analytics results for transactional reads.

acceptance_criteria.text: User documentation for analytical queries states the absence of freshness and cross-shard snapshot guarantees.
Every analytical query result includes the per-shard replication positions it read from.

data.title: Multi-document cross-shard transactions
data.statement: The system shall commit or abort atomically all writes of a transaction spanning multiple documents and shards.
data.rationale: HTAP OLTP workloads need multi-entity atomic updates.

acceptance_criteria.text: A transaction writing documents on 3 different shards, with a coordinator crash injected at each commit phase, leaves either all or none of the writes visible after recovery (100 trials).

data.title: Transactional secondary indexes
data.statement: The system shall maintain secondary indexes on document fields within the same transaction as the document write.
data.rationale: Asynchronous indexes would violate serializable reads through indexes.

acceptance_criteria.text: A query via a secondary index issued after a transaction commits returns that transaction's writes.
A unique secondary index rejects a duplicate value across shards with a constraint-violation error.

data.title: Online index and schema changes
data.statement: The system shall build and drop secondary indexes and attach or change collection schemas without blocking concurrent reads or writes.
data.rationale: Schema evolution must not consume the availability budget.

acceptance_criteria.text: Building an index on a 100 GiB collection under YCSB workload A causes zero failed client requests and OLTP p99 stays within its target +50%.
An in-progress index build can be cancelled and leaves no partial index visible to queries.

data.title: Automatic shard split and rebalance
data.statement: The system shall automatically split shards exceeding a configurable size and rebalance shard replicas across nodes without rejecting client requests.
data.rationale: Horizontal scalability; splits are a common source of correctness bugs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding a node to a cluster under YCSB workload A results in replica counts per node within ±10% of the mean within 1 hour, with zero failed client requests.
The Jepsen-style suite with continuous splits finds zero serializability anomalies.

data.title: Operational telemetry
data.statement: The system shall export metrics and traces via OpenTelemetry covering request latency, commit latency, WAL fsync latency, transaction abort rate, leader changes and analytics-replica replication lag.
data.rationale: Operators need visibility, particularly of analytics lag since it carries no SLA.

acceptance_criteria.text: An OpenTelemetry collector receives each listed metric from every node at least every 15 seconds.
Analytics replication lag per shard is exported in seconds and in log entries.

data.title: Encryption in transit
data.statement: The system shall encrypt 100% of client and intra-cluster connections using TLS 1.3 or TLS 1.2 restricted to AEAD cipher suites.
data.rationale: NIST SP 800-52r2 baseline.

acceptance_criteria.text: A TLS scanner against client and peer ports reports no SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 or non-AEAD cipher suites.
A plaintext connection attempt to a client or peer port is refused.

data.title: Mutual TLS between cluster nodes
data.statement: The system shall refuse 100% of intra-cluster connections not authenticated by a valid cluster certificate.
data.rationale: Prevents rogue nodes joining or impersonating peers.

acceptance_criteria.text: A peer connection presenting no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate from another CA is refused and audit-logged.

data.title: Authentication required by default
data.statement: The system shall require authentication for every client connection by default, supporting SCRAM-SHA-256, x.509 client certificates and OIDC tokens.
data.rationale: Unauthenticated defaults are the commonest real-world database breach.

acceptance_criteria.text: A freshly installed node rejects unauthenticated connections and listens only on loopback until explicitly configured otherwise.
A client can authenticate successfully with each of SCRAM-SHA-256, x.509 and OIDC.

data.title: Role-based access control
data.statement: The system shall deny 100% of operations not permitted by the requesting principal's roles, with privileges scoped to individual collections.
data.rationale: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 access-control evidence; least-privilege built-in roles.

acceptance_criteria.text: A user granted read on collection A receives a permission error on any write to A and any read of collection B.
Built-in roles (read, readWrite, dbAdmin, clusterAdmin) are documented with their exact privileges.

data.title: Encryption at rest
data.statement: The system shall encrypt data files, WAL, backups and analytics replicas at rest with AES-256 using data keys wrapped by a KMS-managed key.
data.rationale: Confidentiality and enables crypto-shredding for erasure.

acceptance_criteria.text: A byte-level scan of data files, WAL segments and backup files finds no plaintext of a known inserted marker value.
Rotating the KMS key does not require downtime and old data remains readable.

data.title: Audit logging
data.statement: The system shall record authentication attempts, authorization failures, DDL and administrative actions in an append-only audit log exportable to an external sink, with document values redacted.
data.rationale: Accountability evidence for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 without retaining PII.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each listed event type produces an audit record with timestamp, principal, action, target and outcome within 5 seconds.
Audit records contain no document field values.

data.title: DS-CORE is a key-value/document store for HTAP workloads
data.context: PO asked to define engine type and workload.
data.decision: Key-value / document data model serving both transactional and analytical (HTAP) workloads.

data.title: Distributed sharded deployment with Raft
data.context: Choice of deployment and consistency model for v1.
data.decision: Shard data across nodes, replicating each shard with Raft for strong consistency.

data.title: Serializable isolation by default
data.context: Isolation level options: snapshot isolation, serializable, single-document only.
data.decision: All transactions run at serializable isolation; accept higher abort rates, mitigated by a retryable error contract.

data.title: Analytics on same-format replicas, eventually consistent
data.context: How to isolate analytics from OLTP and how fresh analytics must be.
data.decision: Dedicated non-voting analytics replicas in row/document format; reads are eventually consistent with no freshness bound.

data.title: PartiQL as primary query API
data.context: Options: MongoDB-compatible, SQL/JSON, PartiQL, native gRPC/REST.
data.decision: PartiQL (SQL++ family) is the primary query and DML language.

impact_notes.stories: None yet — this is the first requirement set. Every requirement will show 'no story' in the trace gate until /reqforge:plan creates epics, stories and evals.
impact_notes.code: No components configured for DS-CORE; no code or trace tags affected.
impact_notes.evals: None yet. Planning must add performance evals (REQ latency, HTAP isolation, size limit), e2e/integration evals for reliability (commit durability, failover, membership, PITR, upgrade, availability), security evals for TLS/mTLS/authn/RBAC/at-rest/audit, and a Jepsen-style correctness suite.
risks: Several thresholds are research defaults awaiting PO confirmation: failover ≤ 10 s, 99.99% availability, RPO ≤ 5 min / 7-day PITR window, ≤ 10% OLTP degradation under analytics, 30-day erasure, 16 MiB document limit.
Open decisions: client transport protocol (gRPC / HTTP/2 / custom) and how a query is marked analytical.
Serializable-by-default will raise abort rates under contention; clients must handle the retryable error.
Eventually consistent analytics means cross-shard aggregates can be momentarily inconsistent with each other and with OLTP.
Five findings are graded THIN (PITR, SLA, JSON Schema, TLS, GDPR, PartiQL) and should be re-verified before external commitments.

Backups older than the delete become unreadable for the deleted data via destruction of the associated encryption key (crypto-shredding) within 30 days.

data.title: Bounded physical erasure
data.statement: The system shall make deleted documents unrecoverable from data files, WAL, replicas and backups within 30 days of deletion.
data.rationale: GDPR Art. 17: deletes in log-structured/replicated engines leave copies in tombstones, WAL, replicas and backups.
data.source: Research default — PO to confirm 30-day bound

acceptance_criteria.text: With default configuration, a 16 MiB document is accepted and a 16 MiB + 1 byte document is rejected with the size-limit error.
Changing the configured limit takes effect without a cluster restart.

data.title: Document size limit
data.statement: The system shall enforce a configurable maximum document size, defaulting to 16 MiB, and reject larger documents with a size-limit error.
data.rationale: Unbounded documents risk memory exhaustion and oversized Raft log entries.

acceptance_criteria.text: No session, collection or client option can lower isolation below serializable; attempts return a configuration error.

A Jepsen-style test (network partitions, node crashes, clock skew, membership changes and shard splits) runs for at least 1 hour per release and an Elle-style checker finds zero serializability anomalies.

data.title: Serializable isolation by default
data.statement: The system shall execute every transaction, including single-statement and cross-shard transactions, at serializable isolation regardless of session, collection or client settings.
data.rationale: PO decision: serializable by default. Jepsen found weak defaults undercutting advertised guarantees (MongoDB 4.2.6).

acceptance_criteria.text: An interactive transaction whose read set changed is never silently retried; the client receives the serialization-conflict error.
The Jepsen-style suite run for at least 1 hour with internal retry enabled reports 0 lost updates.

data.title: Safe internal transaction retry
data.statement: The system shall produce 0 lost updates and 0 serializability anomalies attributable to internal transaction retry.
data.rationale: TiDB's auto-retry caused lost updates and read skew (Jepsen 2.1.7). Retries that cannot preserve serializability must surface the serialization-conflict error instead.

acceptance_criteria.text: After power-cutting all nodes of a 3-voter shard immediately after acknowledgment, every acknowledged write is present on restart (1,000 trials, zero losses).
With only one voter plus any number of analytics replicas reachable, writes to that shard are not acknowledged.

data.title: Durable quorum commit
data.statement: The system shall lose 0 acknowledged writes when every node loses power simultaneously, acknowledging a write only after a majority of the shard's voting replicas have fsynced it.
data.rationale: Prevents loss of acknowledged writes on correlated power loss. Analytics replicas never count toward the quorum.

acceptance_criteria.text: Under the Jepsen-style suite with continuous add/remove of replicas, no two leaders are observed in the same term for a shard.
A newly added replica is not counted as a voter until its log lag is below the configured bound.

data.title: Safe membership change
data.statement: The system shall keep at most 1 leader per shard per Raft term in 100% of voter membership changes, using joint consensus or single-server changes.
data.rationale: Single-step multi-voter changes can produce split majorities. New replicas join as non-voting learners and are promoted after catch-up.

acceptance_criteria.text: Across 100 leader-node kills in a 3-AZ cluster, p99 time from kill to first successful write on the affected shard is ≤ 10 s.
Configuration validation rejects election timeouts less than 10× the measured heartbeat round trip.

data.title: Leader failover time
data.statement: The system shall elect a new shard leader and resume serving writes within 10 seconds (p99) of the current leader's node failing.
data.rationale: Bounds write unavailability per shard; research found no verified industry figure.
data.source: Research — PO to confirm 10 s bound

acceptance_criteria.text: Availability is measured per calendar month as the fraction of 1-minute intervals in which a synthetic probe's read and write both succeed, and is ≥ 99.99%.
Loss of one full availability zone causes no interval of unavailability longer than the failover bound.

data.title: Regional availability SLA
data.statement: The system shall achieve at least 99.99% monthly availability for a regional deployment spanning 3 availability zones.
data.rationale: Research default aligned with Spanner regional SLA structure; 99.999% reserved for future multi-region.

acceptance_criteria.text: After destroying the cluster, restoring to a chosen timestamp recovers all transactions committed at least 5 minutes before the loss.
Restore throughput is measured and published per node, and the documented RTO formula predicts measured restore time within 20%.

data.title: Point-in-time recovery
data.statement: The system shall restore a cluster to any chosen timestamp within a 7-day retention window, losing no more than 5 minutes of committed transactions.
data.rationale: Quorum replication gives RPO 0 against node loss but not against operator error or corruption.

acceptance_criteria.text: During a rolling upgrade under YCSB workload A, the synthetic probe records no failed interval and OLTP p99 stays within its target +50%.
A mixed-version cluster of N and N+1 minor versions passes the transaction test suite.

data.title: Rolling upgrade without downtime
data.statement: The system shall upgrade one node at a time between consecutive minor versions while continuing to serve reads and writes, transferring shard leadership off each node before it stops.
data.rationale: Planned maintenance must not consume the availability budget.

acceptance_criteria.text: YCSB workloads A, B, C and F run for 30 minutes each at 70% of rated throughput; p99 read latency ≤ 10 ms.
In the same runs, p99 write (update/read-modify-write) latency ≤ 20 ms.

data.title: OLTP point read/write latency
data.statement: The system shall serve single-document point reads within 10 ms and point writes within 20 ms at the 99th percentile in a 3-AZ single-region deployment on SSD storage, at 70% of rated cluster throughput.
data.rationale: PO decision on p99 targets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Running YCSB workload A concurrently with a CH-benCHmark-style analytical load at 100% analytics-replica CPU, OLTP p99 read and write latency increase by no more than 10% versus the same YCSB run without analytics.

data.title: OLTP latency under analytical load
data.statement: The system shall keep OLTP p99 latency within 10% of its no-analytics baseline while analytical queries saturate the analytics replicas.
data.rationale: The purpose of dedicated analytics replicas is workload isolation.
data.source: Research default — PO to confirm 10% bound

acceptance_criteria.text: An analytical query is never executed on a voting replica; tracing shows only analytics replicas served it.
If no analytics replica is available, an analytical query fails with an explicit error rather than falling back to voting replicas.

data.title: Analytics on dedicated replicas
data.statement: The system shall execute queries marked analytical only on dedicated non-voting analytics replicas that store data in the same row/document format as voting replicas.
data.rationale: PO decision: dedicated same-format analytics replicas.
data.notes: Open: how a query is marked analytical (hint, session, separate endpoint).

acceptance_criteria.text: User documentation for analytical queries states the absence of freshness and cross-shard snapshot guarantees.
Every analytical query result includes the per-shard replication positions it read from.

data.title: Eventual consistency of analytics reads
data.statement: The system shall document that analytics-replica reads are eventually consistent, with no freshness bound and no cross-shard snapshot guarantee.
data.rationale: PO decision: eventual, no freshness guarantee. Users must not mistake analytics results for transactional reads.

acceptance_criteria.text: A transaction writing documents on 3 different shards, with a coordinator crash injected at each commit phase, leaves either all or none of the writes visible after recovery (100 trials).

data.title: Multi-document cross-shard transactions
data.statement: The system shall commit or abort atomically all writes of a transaction spanning multiple documents and shards.
data.rationale: HTAP OLTP workloads need multi-entity atomic updates.

acceptance_criteria.text: A query via a secondary index issued after a transaction commits returns that transaction's writes.
A unique secondary index rejects a duplicate value across shards with a constraint-violation error.

data.title: Transactional secondary indexes
data.statement: The system shall maintain secondary indexes on document fields within the same transaction as the document write.
data.rationale: Asynchronous indexes would violate serializable reads through indexes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Building an index on a 100 GiB collection under YCSB workload A causes zero failed client requests and OLTP p99 stays within its target +50%.
An in-progress index build can be cancelled and leaves no partial index visible to queries.

data.title: Online index and schema changes
data.statement: The system shall build and drop secondary indexes and attach or change collection schemas without blocking concurrent reads or writes.
data.rationale: Schema evolution must not consume the availability budget.

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding a node to a cluster under YCSB workload A results in replica counts per node within ±10% of the mean within 1 hour, with zero failed client requests.
The Jepsen-style suite with continuous splits finds zero serializability anomalies.

data.title: Automatic shard split and rebalance
data.statement: The system shall automatically split shards exceeding a configurable size and rebalance shard replicas across nodes without rejecting client requests.
data.rationale: Horizontal scalability; splits are a common source of correctness bugs.

acceptance_criteria.text: An OpenTelemetry collector receives each listed metric from every node at least every 15 seconds.
Analytics replication lag per shard is exported in seconds and in log entries.

data.title: Operational telemetry
data.statement: The system shall export metrics and traces via OpenTelemetry covering request latency, commit latency, WAL fsync latency, transaction abort rate, leader changes and analytics-replica replication lag.
data.rationale: Operators need visibility, particularly of analytics lag since it carries no SLA.

acceptance_criteria.text: A TLS scanner against client and peer ports reports no SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 or non-AEAD cipher suites.
A plaintext connection attempt to a client or peer port is refused.

data.title: Encryption in transit
data.statement: The system shall encrypt 100% of client and intra-cluster connections using TLS 1.3 or TLS 1.2 restricted to AEAD cipher suites.
data.rationale: NIST SP 800-52r2 baseline.

acceptance_criteria.text: A peer connection presenting no certificate, an expired certificate or a certificate from another CA is refused and audit-logged.

data.title: Mutual TLS between cluster nodes
data.statement: The system shall refuse 100% of intra-cluster connections not authenticated by a valid cluster certificate.
data.rationale: Prevents rogue nodes joining or impersonating peers.

acceptance_criteria.text: A freshly installed node rejects unauthenticated connections and listens only on loopback until explicitly configured otherwise.
A client can authenticate successfully with each of SCRAM-SHA-256, x.509 and OIDC.

data.title: Authentication required by default
data.statement: The system shall require authentication for every client connection by default, supporting SCRAM-SHA-256, x.509 client certificates and OIDC tokens.
data.rationale: Unauthenticated defaults are the commonest real-world database breach.

acceptance_criteria.text: A user granted read on collection A receives a permission error on any write to A and any read of collection B.
Built-in roles (read, readWrite, dbAdmin, clusterAdmin) are documented with their exact privileges.

data.title: Role-based access control
data.statement: The system shall deny 100% of operations not permitted by the requesting principal's roles, with privileges scoped to individual collections.
data.rationale: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 access-control evidence; least-privilege built-in roles.

acceptance_criteria.text: A byte-level scan of data files, WAL segments and backup files finds no plaintext of a known inserted marker value.
Rotating the KMS key does not require downtime and old data remains readable.

data.title: Encryption at rest
data.statement: The system shall encrypt data files, WAL, backups and analytics replicas at rest with AES-256 using data keys wrapped by a KMS-managed key.
data.rationale: Confidentiality and enables crypto-shredding for erasure.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each listed event type produces an audit record with timestamp, principal, action, target and outcome within 5 seconds.
Audit records contain no document field values.

data.title: Audit logging
data.statement: The system shall record authentication attempts, authorization failures, DDL and administrative actions in an append-only audit log exportable to an external sink, with document values redacted.
data.rationale: Accountability evidence for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 without retaining PII.

ops.title: DS-CORE is a key-value/document store for HTAP workloads

data.title: DS-CORE is a key-value/document store for HTAP workloads
data.context: PO asked to define engine type and workload.
data.decision: Key-value / document data model serving both transactional and analytical (HTAP) workloads.

data.title: Distributed sharded deployment with Raft
data.context: Choice of deployment and consistency model for v1.
data.decision: Shard data across nodes, replicating each shard with Raft for strong consistency.

data.title: Serializable isolation by default
data.context: Isolation level options: snapshot isolation, serializable, single-document only.
data.decision: All transactions run at serializable isolation; accept higher abort rates, mitigated by a retryable error contract.

ops.title: Analytics on same-format replicas, eventually consistent

data.title: Analytics on same-format replicas, eventually consistent
data.context: How to isolate analytics from OLTP and how fresh analytics must be.
data.decision: Dedicated non-voting analytics replicas in row/document format; reads are eventually consistent with no freshness bound.

data.title: PartiQL as primary query API
data.context: Options: MongoDB-compatible, SQL/JSON, PartiQL, native gRPC/REST.
data.decision: PartiQL (SQL++ family) is the primary query and DML language.
